chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A prescribed prayer is better than twenty pilgrimages, and a pilgrimage is better than a house full of gold which is spent in charity until it is exhausted.

He said, then he said: 'And he will not succeed who loses twenty houses of gold for twenty-five dirhams.' I said: 'What is the meaning of twenty-five?' He said: 'Whoever withholds the zakat, his prayer is halted until he pays the zakat.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of withholding zakat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes a spiritual hierarchy where the foundational act of obligatory prayer outweighs the cumulative merit of twenty pilgrimages, which in turn surpasses the charity of a 'house full of gold.' The Imam’s subsequent clarification links the withholding of *zakat* directly to the suspension of *salah*, illustrating the Shia scholarly view that financial obligations are not merely social duties but integral to the validity of ritual worship. This interconnection underscores the holistic nature of worship in Shia jurisprudence, where ritual purity and financial piety are mutually reinforcing.
